source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 8 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: Converting a fraction to a decimal may give an infinite decimal where a group of digits repeats; it is called repeating and the group is the period.
stages.headlineEnglish: Converting a fraction to a decimal may give an infinite decimal where a group of digits repeats; it is called repeating and the group is the period.

stages.headline: A reduced fraction gives a finite decimal if its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5; otherwise it repeats.
stages.headlineEnglish: A reduced fraction gives a finite decimal if its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5; otherwise it repeats.

stages.headline: To turn a repeating decimal into a fraction: x = 0.(45), 100x = 45.(45), 99x = 45, x = 45/99 = 5/11.
stages.headlineEnglish: To turn a repeating decimal into a fraction: x = 0.(45), 100x = 45.(45), 99x = 45, x = 45/99 = 5/11.
